_meanings:
.²1 Consciousness; {#akaruRa punaH saMjYAvyADiM viDAya kimIhase#} <ls>Māl. 9. 42</ls>;
 {#ratiKedasamutpannA nidrA saMjYAviparyayaH#} <ls>Ku. 6. 44</ls>. {#saMjYAM#}
 {#laB, Apad#} or {#pratipad#} ‘to regain or recover oneʼs consciousness,
 come to oneʼs senses’.
.²2 Knowledge, understanding; {#nAyakA mama sEnyasya saMjYArTaM tAn bravImi#}
 {#te#} <ls>Bg. 1. 7</ls>; <ls>Mb. 12. 153. 63</ls>.
.²3 Intellect, mind; {#lokatantraM hi saMjYASca sarvamanne pratizWitam#} <ls>Mb. 13. 63. 5</ls>.
.²4 A hint, sign, token, gesture; {#muKArpitEkANgulisaMjYayEva mA cApalAyeti#}
 {#gaRAn vyanEzIt#} <ls>Ku. 3. 41</ls>; {#upalaBya tataSca DarmasaMjYAm#} <ls>Bu. Ch. 5. 21</ls>;
 <ls>Bhāg. 6. 7. 17</ls>.
.²5 A name, designation, an appellation; <ab>oft.</ab> at the end of <ab>comp.</ab> in this
 sense; {#dvandvErvimuktAH suKaduHKasaMjYEH#} <ls>Bg. 15. 5</ls>.
.²6 (In <ab>gram.</ab>) Any name or noun having a special meaning, a proper name.
.²7 The technical name for an affix.
.²8 The Gāyatrī Mantra; see {#gAyatrI#}.
.²9 A track, footstep.
.²10 Direction.
.²11 A technical term.
.²12 <ab>N.</ab> of the daughter of Viśvakarman and wife of the sun, and mother
 of Yama, Yamī, and the two Aśvins. [A legend relates that {#saMjYA#}
 on one occasion wished to go to her fatherʼs house and asked her husbandʼs
 permission, which was not granted. Resolved to carry out her purpose,
 she created, by means of her superhuman power, a woman exactly like herself
 --who was, as it were, her own shadow (and was therefore called Chhāyā),
 --and putting her in her own place, went away without the knowledge of
 the sun. Chhāyā bore to the sun three children (see {#CAyA#}), and lived
 quite happily with him, so that when Saṃjñā returned, he would not
 admit her. Thus repudiated and disappointed, she assumed the form of a
 mare and roamed over the earth. The sun, however, in course of time, came
 to know the real state of things, and discovered that his wife had assumed
 the form of a mare. He accordingly assumed the form of a horse, and was
 united with his wife, who bore to him, two sons-- the Aśvinīkumāras
 or Aśvins <ab>q. v.</ab>]

a leading rule which gives a particular name to the
 rules falling under it, and which exercises influence over them.
any Sūtra which teaches the meaning of a technical term.
